sentences.text:
Claim Case No. 50/2011; whereby appellant/claimant has been awarded a sum of Rs.2,23,000/-
alongwith interest as compensation for the injuries sustained by appellant in a road accident dated 20/4/2009.
The liability of payment of compensation amount was fastened over respondents No. 1 and 2 and respondent no. 3/Insurance Company was exonerated from payment of compensation amount.

By filing this appeal, appellant has prayed for shifting of liability over the Insurance Company in light of Decision of Apex Court in the matter of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,
2017 ACJ 2011.

entities.text:
Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,
2017 ACJ 2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the question of shifting of liability over the Insurance Company is concerned, while passing the impugned award,learned Claim Tribunal shifted the burden of payment of impugned award over respondents No. 1 and 2 while exonerating Insurance Company on the ground that on the date of incident, respondent No. 1-Driver was not having valid and effective driving licence for driving transport vehicle - Auto as he was having LMV licence.

The aforesaid controversy has been put to rest by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra) while holding that "a person holding driving licence to drive 'light motor vehicle'
is competent to drive transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kgs or a motor car, tractor or road-roller, the unladen weight of which does not exceed 7.500 kgs."
Undisputedly, the respondent No. 1 was holding a LMV licence at the time of incident and was driving a transport/passenger vehicle, whose unladen vehicle weight in the instance case as per submission of parties is below 7,500 kgs and therefore, in light of aforesaid decision the finding given by Claims Tribunal regarding liability of payment of compensation amount is modified to the extent that now Insurance Company shall make the payment of compensation amount instead of respondents No. 1 and 2 jointly and severally as per impugned award within two months from today.
Rest of the conditions as imposed of Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
Appeal stands partly allowed with the aforesaid modification in impugned award.
(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
